The apple measures about 125 px across against a plate of about 345 px. That gives 125/345 × 25 ≈ 9 cm, which seems a bit large, so I take the apple as about 8 cm in diameter.

**STEP 3 - Items:** One red-yellow apple. There is no other food. The small orange speck on the plate is a crumb or stain and is negligible.

**STEP 6 - Grams:** A whole apple has a density of about 0.8 g/ml, which gives about 200 g. That includes the core, which is part of the visible fruit.

**STEP 7 - Energy:** Apple provides about 52 kcal per 100 g, so 200 g gives about 104 kcal.

**STEP 8 - Sanity check:** A medium apple weighs 180–200 g and has about 95–105 kcal, so the estimate is plausible.
